content/read_bytes/list_dir answer null for a missing path and the empty value for a present empty one; no rule states a file operation's failure answers (see 296)
a live list_dir vector keeps every entry across file reads in its loop at each of two listings; a read must not take a store the listing still holds, and nothing leaks
const parameter/local reads and the #lock attribute's read-back; no write to a locked or const value is attempted, so H-WriteLocked and Const-Value are not exercised - a smoke of the lock attribute

a closure capturing a parameter, a projection or a loop element must not free the caller's store; an owned capture is freed once by the record (escaping factory too); mutated scalar captures write back

an index key typed by a function declared lower in the file (loop iterable, direct call, untyped local, text key, multi-key) answers as if the callee were declared first; no rule states that declaration order does not matter (see 371)
a closure mutating a captured scalar PARAMETER (integer, float, boolean, character, text) shares the write with the enclosing frame, keeps the declared type, and leaves the caller's value untouched

closures capturing projections of a struct declared later read the right values; a mutated forward capture writes back; the World survives every closure; the declaration-order half has no rule (see Decl-Order)
a closure mutating a captured text parameter or local in a text-returning function shares the writes (axy, got:axy, AXY, ax|sy) and the caller's text stays untouched
a local returned on one branch is freed on every path that returns something else (struct, collection, nested, loop, late mint, recursion), called 20x each under the leak gate
range slices over sorted and index with both, open-start, open-end and fully open bounds, integer and text keys, empty collections and rev, hand-computed; single-key lookup unaffected
an element bind through ?? inside a loop is a borrow: its rebind must not free the previous round's store (250, 1500, every field), no leak, and a write through it reaches the source
a #native declaration with no library loaded fails at the call with 'native function not loaded'; packaging behaviour, no formal language rule
a &File parameter is used exactly like a File (#read, #format =, +=, #exists) and its whole-value rebind reaches the caller's handle
a record a callee publishes through a & parameter survives the callee's exit (adopt, fresh, conditional, twice, loop, text field, &File) while an unpublished buffer is still freed
a struct holding a vector returned by value; fields of inline structs read through vector elements at their own offsets after an append; ** gives the root

xs = g.c copies, so an element view written through leaves the source; a read-only view reads the element; an escaping element is an independent value (near-duplicate of 25-index-elision-borrower.loft)

an element read from a keyed collection (hash, index, sorted, trie, any key arity, tuple key) is a view of its container, so returning it from a call-built container materialises a copy; a parameter's container stays borrowed and intact

loops that write no store read the same elements with the vector header held once; loops that grow, shrink, rebind or write through a callee keep re-deriving and read the moved elements; negative and out-of-range indices inside
an element read through a field of a call's result (vector, hash, index, trie, a field of a field, bound then returned, in a loop) is a view of that result, materialised on return; no work-ref growth
sizeof over primitives, enums, a padded struct (24), narrow integers, and collection and reference fields (4-byte collection pointer, 12-byte reference)
